Completing project safely and within required accuracy and timeframe.
Coordinating with survey team and design team to ensure survey scope is clear and deliverable expectations are met.
Assist in developing a plan of action for assigned projects.
Adhering to existing standards of practice for surveying.

Accurately measure angles, distances and other information in conformance with regulations and company standards.
Assist in conducting surveys to establish legal boundaries for properties, based on legal deeds and titles.
Assist in establishing construction control points for use in the installation of equipment and materials.
Searching legal records, survey records, and land titles to obtain information about property boundaries in areas to be surveyed.

jobs.description:

Skydio is looking for seasoned Public Safety sUAS professionals to join our team of Solutions Engineers. We sit between the agency and the product: turning operational problems into program designs, proving capability in the field, and making sure Skydio's products are used, integrated, and flown at scale.

The team is measured on technical win rate, trial and proof of concept outcomes, program expansion, site assessment quality, and the requirements we push back into the product organization.

Strong understanding of drone technology, Public Safety sUAS operations, and regulatory compliance.
Familiarity with Drone as First Responder concepts of operation and dock based remote operations. Professional experience is strongly preferred.
Working knowledge of public safety software platforms, including CAD and VMS, and of API integrations.
Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to think critically in high-pressure situations.
Exceptional written and verbal communication. You can brief an operator, a program manager, and a chief or a city council without changing the facts.
Comfort operating inside a Sales organization, including the judgment to know when to commit technical time and when to decline.

Nice to Have

Prior public safety service as a sworn officer, firefighter, or agency UAS program lead.
Experience standing up a Drone as First Responder program from waiver through go-live, and with dock-based, remote, and BVLOS operations at scale.

The Department of Energy and Envrionmental Protection (DEEP), Emergency Response and Spill Prevention Division has an exciting opportunity for an Environmental Analyst 1 in the Corrective Action Unit. We are seeking an enthusiastic and engaging person to fill a role in a fast-paced environment!

The State of Connecticut is an eligible Public Service Loan Forgiveness employer, meaning you may be eligible to have qualifying student loans forgiven after 10 years of service. Click here for more information.

Position Highlights

As an Environmental Analyst 1 with Corrective Action Unit (CAU), you will receive on-the-job training in the Release Based Cleanup Regulations, investigation and remediation of releases to the environment. Duties include tracking the remediation of Emergent Reportable Releases, reviewing investigation plans and reports, reviewing cleanup plans and reports, evaluating for cleanup compliance, and providing technical support to other DEEP Programs.
The Corrective Action Unit plays a key role in Emergency Response and Spill Prevention Division by tracking, guiding, and ensuring the cleanup progression of many types of releases to the environment and assuring compliance with state regulations.
This is a hybrid full-time position located at the DEEP Headquarters in Hartford, Connecticut.
The schedule is 35 hours per week, Monday through Friday. Typical hours will be 7:30 A.M. to 3:30 P.M. or 8:00 A.M. to 4:00 P.M. with a possible flex schedule upon completion of the working test period.

The Successful Candidate Will

Track Emergent Reportable Releases in DEEP’s Release, Environmental Assessment, and Cleanup Tracker (REACT);
Review and/or oversee the investigation and remediation of Emergent Reportable Releases including releases of PCBs, oil and petroleum, Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), and releases from residential UST systems;
Evaluate work conducted to remediate releases to ensure compliance with applicable environmental statutes, regulations, and written guidance;
Review and evaluate compliance reports and other documents submitted in response to enforcement actions, including documentation related to supplemental environmental projects and in response to remedial cleanup requirements;
Provide technical assistance to the public and the regulated community;
Provide technical consultation to municipal, regional, state, and federal officials and the public;
Perform database maintenance and disseminating and managing information;
Assist in drafting new regulations, statutes, guidelines, and other written materials;
Other tasks as necessary to meet the statutory responsibilities of the Department involving inspection, permitting and enforcement.

Job Duties

The CAU assists in fulfilling the DEEP’s critical mission of restoration, protection, and conservation of Connecticut’s water and land resources and protection of public health and safety. The CAU tracks the cleanup progress of Emergent Reportable Releases, reviews and approves remedial strategies completed pursuant to formal and informal enforcement actions and spill responses, reviews investigation and cleanup plans, reviews fields investigations and tracks state cleanup compliance, and tracks federal polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB) and leaking Underground Storage Tank (UST) grant requirements.

About Us

Nearly every day, despite preventative measures, there are incidents that threaten the environment. The State of Connecticut, Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP), Bureau of Materials Management and Compliance Assurance’s Emergency Response and Spill Prevention Division is prepared to limit the risks and handle incidents ranging from a spill of a few gallons to a tanker full of petroleum liquids, from abandoned or leaking underground storage tank or unknown drums of chemicals to anthrax or a chemical fire.

Releases, even small ones, can endanger public health or the environment by making the water or air unsafe. Releases of hazardous materials can contaminate surface water, groundwater or soil, impact plants, fish and wildlife and their habitats, or create unsafe exposure to the general public or emergency responders.

The Emergency Response and Spill Prevention Division responses 24 hours per day to emergencies that result from accidental and deliberate discharges and uncontrolled releases of oil, petroleum, hazardous wastes and chemicals to the air, land and waterways from roadway incidents, industrial processes, oil and chemical spills, failed tanks/pipes and abandoned drums as well as biological and chemical weapons.

The Division Is Also Responsible For

Coordinating state and local emergency planning and preparedness activities and public disclosure information as required by federal and state law;
Regulating, inspecting and taking necessary enforcement actions to ensure the safety of underground storage tanks;
Investigating potential risks to surface water, groundwater or soil;
Permitting marine terminals;
Overseeing the completion of spill cleanups and conducting enforcement related to these activities.

Position Highlights

As an Environmental Analyst 1 with Corrective Action Unit (CAU), you will receive on-the-job training in the Release Based Cleanup Regulations, investigation and remediation of releases to the environment. Duties include tracking the remediation of Emergent Reportable Releases, reviewing investigation plans and reports, reviewing cleanup plans and reports, evaluating for cleanup compliance, and providing technical support to other DEEP Programs.
The Corrective Action Unit plays a key role in Emergency Response and Spill Prevention Division by tracking, guiding, and ensuring the cleanup progression of many types of releases to the environment and assuring compliance with state regulations.
This is a hybrid full-time position located at the DEEP Headquarters in Hartford, Connecticut.
The schedule is 35 hours per week, Monday through Friday. Typical hours will be 7:30 A.M. to 3:30 P.M. or 8:00 A.M. to 4:00 P.M. with a possible flex schedule upon completion of the working test period.

The Successful Candidate Will

Track Emergent Reportable Releases in DEEP’s Release, Environmental Assessment, and Cleanup Tracker (REACT);
Review and/or oversee the investigation and remediation of Emergent Reportable Releases including releases of PCBs, oil and petroleum, Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), and releases from residential UST systems;
Evaluate work conducted to remediate releases to ensure compliance with applicable environmental statutes, regulations, and written guidance;
Review and evaluate compliance reports and other documents submitted in response to enforcement actions, including documentation related to supplemental environmental projects and in response to remedial cleanup requirements;
Provide technical assistance to the public and the regulated community;
Provide technical consultation to municipal, regional, state, and federal officials and the public;
Perform database maintenance and disseminating and managing information;
Assist in drafting new regulations, statutes, guidelines, and other written materials;
Other tasks as necessary to meet the statutory responsibilities of the Department involving inspection, permitting and enforcement.

Job Duties

The CAU assists in fulfilling the DEEP’s critical mission of restoration, protection, and conservation of Connecticut’s water and land resources and protection of public health and safety. The CAU tracks the cleanup progress of Emergent Reportable Releases, reviews and approves remedial strategies completed pursuant to formal and informal enforcement actions and spill responses, reviews investigation and cleanup plans, reviews fields investigations and tracks state cleanup compliance, and tracks federal polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB) and leaking Underground Storage Tank (UST) grant requirements.

About Us

Nearly every day, despite preventative measures, there are incidents that threaten the environment. What if every moment of play could unlock measurable developmental breakthroughs?

At Alpha, education looks nothing like the traditional model. Our PreK program blends play-based curriculum design with real-time developmental data — no rigid lesson scripts, no compliance checklists. You will design adaptive learning themes across every readiness domain, coach a team of Guides to deliver them with precision and joy, and track measurable milestone progress for every child in the cohort.

The rest is designing curriculum, coaching Guides with specific, measurable goals, and keeping families informed with evidence-based updates. You will see the direct impact of your work: four-year-olds hitting developmental milestones faster, Guides improving their quality scores week over week, and parents becoming advocates.

Coach the Guides. Design the play. Apply now.

What You Will Be Doing

Lead 1:1 and small-group coaching sessions for PreK Guides, modeling techniques, and celebrating measurable wins
Design and facilitate play-based learning blocks that balance SEL, literacy, numeracy, and motor skills, modeling best-in-class practice for the team
Review and calibrate Guide documentation weekly for rubric alignment and actionability, leading calibration sessions to keep milestone progress visible
Prepare family updates and run team huddles that align priorities and reinforce shared expectations toward campus-wide PreK readiness goals

What You Won’t Be Doing

Rigid lesson scripts or compliance-driven routines have no place here — you'll design adaptive, play-based themes that respond to real data
Teaching to a fixed curriculum handed down from above — you own the quarterly and weekly learning design
Working in isolation without feedback loops — coaching conversations and calibration sessions are built into every week
Managing K-12 students on app-based learning — this role is fully dedicated to early childhood, hands-on, in-the-room work

Preschool Program Coordinator Key Responsibilities

Drive campus-wide PreK readiness outcomes through guide coaching, program fidelity, and joyful, data-driven classrooms.

Basic Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Psychology, or related field; Master's or specialized training preferred
At least 5 years of professional experience working directly with children ages 3 to 5, including as a lead or primary teacher in a classroom or structured program
Proven ability to design and implement play-based educational programs or curricula that advance developmental milestones e.g. Montessori
At least 1 year of experience coaching or managing a team of educators with performance accountability
Experience preparing written family progress updates and leading team alignment meetings in an educational setting
Legally authorized to work in the United States without visa sponsorship
Willingness to work in-person at Alpha Austin campus with relocation support provided if needed

Nice-to-have Requirements

Familiarity with edtech platforms, adaptive dashboards, or digital observation tools used in early childhood settings
Experience with behavior guidance strategies and co-regulation techniques for children ages 3-5
